verified.notes: Packed tarball 0.1.1 (market install verified end to end at 81dd43b) (sha256 d7cf20df57c56e6dac84eb58014c1e369cdde94bf2612456ed030031c7bb7d18) installed into an owned, disposable, non-Desktop web profile created from the shipped template (DSH 0.2.1-rc.5). dsh --profile <test> --dump-config composed the bundle row; a bounded real startup served the Web app; the authenticated browser transport exercised the exact /api/skillre-sticky-wall/execute route (list, create, update, archive, delete) and a second startup proved the note survived a restart through the storage domain. An unauthenticated request to the same route returned 401, so Connection still fences it. Cleanup stopped every owned process, removed the owned profile root and verified it was gone. The real DSH Web UI was then driven in headless Chromium against the same owned profile: the 便签墙 sidebar entry appeared and selected the panel, the wall mounted with the seeded welcome note, the composer created a blue note, pin moved it first, search filtered to it, archive hid it from the default wall, the archived toggle showed it again, the note survived a full page reload, and the dark theme re-styled every card. 15/15 UI assertions passed with no uncaught errors (docs/evidence/ui-verification.json plus four screenshots). Cleanup stopped every owned process, removed the owned profile and Chromium scratch directories and verified both were gone. The published market entry was then verified end to end: the LIVE hosted index (https://skillre.github.io/dsh-plugin-market/index.json) was fetched, its own install spec (git+https://github.com/skillre/dsh-plugin-sticky-wall.git#81dd43be65bd821b92ea4305a4f1cce392985c0e) was installed into a fresh owned profile, --dump-config composed the row, a bounded startup served the app and the route answered; the same-origin icon returned 200. Cleanup removed the owned profile and verified it was gone.

observations.pendingDetail: Verified in the standalone DSH Web application. The Desktop Client (Electron) was not exercised: its profile is managed by the application and cannot be driven by this CLI-based harness. A Desktop-targeted release must repeat the visual check there.
